newCard.subject: History
newCard.name: Canadian treaty agreements and historical effects
newCard.description: Identify a few studied regional agreements involving Indigenous peoples around1780–1850, explain particular parties, commitments and historical effects on communities, and relate an accurately attributed wampum record or continuing agreement relationship to its own purpose and chronology. Distinguish the agreements rather than assuming identical terms or that a present reserve boundary establishes their meaning.
evidence: After studying a verified regional case set, identify selected agreements and their parties and period; explain a specific supported commitment and effect for the communities involved.

Compare agreements with different purposes or terms and distinguish an agreement’s promises from documented subsequent events. Explain an attributed wampum record/relationship without treating it merely as decoration, money or a belt necessarily exchanged for every land agreement.

Keep an earlier continuing wampum relationship chronologically distinct from1780–1850 agreements. Apply the distinction to a further verified agreement/record, using its own source rather than importing the first case’s terms or adjudicating current rights.
newCard.assessmentPrompt: After studying a few regional agreements, can {{name}} identify who made them, what a particular agreement promised and how it affected the communities? Compare two with different purposes or terms. Using an attributed account of a wampum belt or relationship, can they explain what it records and when it began, without assuming every agreement had the same terms or every belt was exchanged at the date of a later land agreement?

pedagogy.summary: Build actual regional historical knowledge with distinct named agreements, attributed perspectives and a simple promise/event comparison. Use existing historical-source reasoning for the method; it does not supply these facts.
bestPractices: Teach a few named, region-relevant agreements and their parties before probing recall and explanation; do not make legal-text decoding the gate.
Compare particular promises with supported subsequent historical events, keeping attribution and uncertainty explicit.
Keep earlier continuing wampum context separate from a later agreement’s date. Do not manufacture a physical exchange for each selected treaty.
keyRepresentations: A source-attributed agreement table: date/place, parties, particular promise and documented historical effect.
A timeline separating earlier relationship origins, selected period agreements and later events.
commonMisconceptions: Every treaty meant the same thing or ended every Indigenous right.
Knowing a treaty number or contemporary reserve name establishes actual terms and effects.
A belt’s earlier origin makes it a newly exchanged object at every later treaty.

learn.summary: Teach a bounded local case repertoire, then compare actual agreement knowledge and a relevant attributed wampum relationship without reducing all treaties to land sales.

activities.title: Particular agreements, promises and consequences
learnerActions: Study adult-prepared, own-word summaries of TorontoPurchase1805, Ajetance1818 and Haldimand1784 in a southern Ontario packet. Locate the relevant broad region using verified references; these examples do not apply uniformly to every Ontario community.

Identify the parties and a particular commitment in each case. Compare the Nation’s accounts of Toronto/Etobicoke fishing and Ajetance annual goods with the Grand River settlement account; avoid assuming one term belongs to every agreement.
Distinguish the commitments from supported historical consequences and later claims or commemorations; explain a real effect for the communities without deciding current legal title.

Study Wiikwemkoong’s own account of1764Niagara promises embedded in wampum and the continuing alliance invoked during1812. Connect those attributed events on the timeline, then distinguish the later1830s displacement/1836context. The earlier wampum is not a newly exchanged1805or1818belt.

Use the separately attributed OnondagaTwoRow account as another earlier continuing relationship when comparing purposes; retain its earlier origin and parallel-path/noninterference meaning. It is not a claim that the same belt was exchanged for each selected land agreement.

After study, reconstruct a simple agreement table and explain a contrast without a completed answer key. Then read a short new verified case and identify which facts need its own evidence rather than assuming the studied terms.
activities.intendedInsight: Actual agreements have particular parties, commitments, purposes and effects; chronology and attributed wampum relationships matter, and agreement terms cannot be inferred from a name or projected from another case.
feedback: Ask who promised what, then which source supports the stated historical effect.
If all agreements are called a complete surrender of every right, return to the particular retained commitment or relationship in the source.
If chronology is collapsed, place the earlier belt relationship and later period agreements on separate timeline entries.
activities.rationale: Original untested historical-knowledge teaching design, not a legal opinion or efficacy claim.
sourceClaims: The Nation describes an uncertain1787agreement, the1805TorontoPurchase, retained Etobicoke Creek fishing and later consequences/claim history.
The Nation describes the1818Ajetanceagreement in its settler-pressure/economic context and a commitment of annual goods; its account does not make all agreements identical.
Six Nations of the Grand River identifies the1784Haldimandagreement with settlement along the Grand River; its contemporary holiday account is not a current parcel-title determination.
Bradley Powless’s attributed Onondaga account dates the Two Row relationship earlier and explains distinct parallel paths, equal relations and noninterference as continuing commitments.

Wiikwemkoong’s own history links1764Niagara promises embedded in wampum with the continuing British alliance invoked during1812, then describes1830s displacement and1836BondHead context. The earlier wampum date remains explicit.

constraints: Use genuinely verified agreements relevant to the selected region; the worked southern Ontario repertoire is not an all-Ontario treaty inventory.
Use accurate adult-prepared summaries and attributed community accounts. Source copies, protected ceremonies, belt replication or pupil disclosure are not required.
No legal-title adjudication, treaty-right eligibility ruling, every treaty article, every wampum design or assumption all treaties were sales/extinguished rights.
Earlier Two Row origin is context, not an invented period exchange. Do not claim a specific belt accompanied Treaty13/19 without evidence.
reviewNotes: 2026-11-10: original source-checked curation following whole-claim comparison and actual A3.7 review. The Canadian wampum case uses the Nation’s explicit1764→1812continuity rather than inventing a later belt exchange. Teaching efficacy remains untested.

assess.diagnosticPrompt: After studying a few regional agreements, can {{name}} identify who made them, what a particular agreement promised and how it affected the communities? Compare two with different purposes or terms. Using an attributed account of a wampum belt or relationship, can they explain what it records and when it began, without assuming every agreement had the same terms or every belt was exchanged at the date of a later land agreement?
assess.correctAnswer: Knows the selected agreements’ actual parties/period, explains supported commitments and historical effects, distinguishes promises from events, and retains the wampum account’s attributed purpose and chronology without importing terms or making current legal judgments.
assess.whatMakesItDiscriminate: Different studied terms rule out a memorized universal treaty story; promise-versus-event separation tests historical relationship knowledge. The explicit earlier wampum→period alliance link exposes chronology conflation, while an unseen case requires its own evidence rather than guessing from a number or map.
probeDeeper: Which part is a commitment, and which is a later event?
Does the source support this claim for this agreement, or only for another one?
What does the attributed belt account record, and is its origin the same date as this selected treaty?

errorPatterns.pattern: Uses a universal land-sale or rights-ended story for every agreement.
errorPatterns.revealedBy: Overrides a stated retained commitment or distinct settlement/peace purpose.
errorPatterns.nextMove: Compare the particular parties and commitments and explain one supported difference.

errorPatterns.pattern: Conflates earlier wampum origin, later agreement and current legal status.
errorPatterns.revealedBy: Invents an1805belt exchange or treats a current reserve map as the treaty’s full meaning.
errorPatterns.nextMove: Rebuild the source-attributed timeline and distinguish historical facts from unestablished present legal conclusions.

responseLevels.gap: Only names a number/place or repeats unsupported universal treaty terms.
responseLevels.partial: Knows some terms/effects but confuses parties, promises/events, agreement differences or chronology.
responseLevels.full: Explains the studied regional agreements and their particular historical relationships, retains attributed wampum chronology, and distinguishes a further case without unsupported transfer of terms.
